title: Ninth Word Fifth Point Human Weakness Impotence And Needs

questions.question: What is the main idea of this passage about human nature?
questions.answer: It shows that human beings are naturally weak, limited, needy, and easily hurt in many ways.

questions.question: How does the passage describe a person’s strength in dealing with life?
questions.answer: It says a person has very little strength and cannot handle everything by himself.

questions.question: What effect do outside events have on a human being in this passage?
questions.answer: Many things affect him deeply and cause sadness, pain, and grief.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the number of hardships and threats a person faces?
questions.answer: It says they are many and surround him from different directions.

questions.question: How are human needs described?
questions.answer: They are described as numerous, showing that people are in need of many things.

questions.question: What contrast is made between human ability and human responsibilities?
questions.answer: A person is shown as weak and not very capable, while the duties of life are heavy.

questions.question: Why does a person feel pain when things around him fade away or disappear?
questions.answer: Because being human connects him to the world and to the things he loves and knows well.

questions.question: What role does reason play in this passage?
questions.answer: Reason makes a person aware of high goals and lasting results.

questions.question: What limits keep a person from fully reaching those high goals?
questions.answer: His ability is limited, his lifespan is short, his strength is small, and his patience is not great.

questions.question: What overall picture of the human condition comes from all these descriptions together?
questions.answer: Human beings need help beyond themselves because they are surrounded by weakness, need, loss, and limitation.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is one basic weakness built into human nature?
questions.answer: A person is naturally very fragile and can be affected by many things.

questions.question: In what emotional way is this weakness shown?
questions.answer: He becomes sorrowful and distressed when things touch his heart.

questions.question: Besides weakness, what does the passage say about human power?
questions.answer: It says human power is very limited.

questions.question: Why is limited power a serious problem in the passage?
questions.answer: Because troubles and enemies are many, so a person cannot easily resist them all.

questions.question: How does the passage describe human neediness?
questions.answer: It presents people as lacking much and needing many things.

questions.question: What does the passage say about human effort and capability in daily life?
questions.answer: It says people are often sluggish and unable to carry life’s heavy burdens well.

questions.question: How does being connected to the universe affect a person emotionally?
questions.answer: It causes pain when familiar and loved things decline or pass away.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the hopes a person carries in his mind?
questions.answer: His mind points him toward noble aims and outcomes that last.

questions.question: Why is there a struggle between those hopes and real life?
questions.answer: Because a person’s reach is limited, his time is short, and his strength and endurance are small.

questions.question: What lesson can a student draw from this passage about self-sufficiency?
questions.answer: A human being should not think he is fully self-sufficient, because his nature is full of weakness and need.

questions.question: Which human qualities are emphasized most in this passage?
questions.answer: Weakness, neediness, limited ability, and emotional vulnerability.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about how easily a person is affected by life?
questions.answer: It suggests that many things impact him and bring him sadness.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the challenges coming against a person?
questions.answer: They are presented as numerous disasters and opponents.

questions.question: What is the relationship between human lack and human needs in the passage?
questions.answer: A person lacks much, yet at the same time he needs many things, which increases his dependence.

questions.question: How does the passage describe a person’s ability to carry out life’s duties?
questions.answer: It says he is not naturally strong enough for all the heavy responsibilities placed on him.

questions.question: Why do changes in the world hurt a person so much?
questions.answer: Because he is tied to the wider world and becomes attached to what he knows and loves.

questions.question: What kind of goals does human reason point toward?
questions.answer: It points toward elevated purposes and results that continue.

questions.question: What four limits are mentioned that make those goals hard to achieve?
questions.answer: Limited reach, short life, small power, and little patience.

questions.question: What tension is found between the human mind and the human condition?
questions.answer: The mind sees great possibilities, but the person himself is too limited to reach them fully on his own.

questions.question: What is the tone of the passage toward human beings?
questions.answer: It is realistic and serious, showing both the dignity of human aims and the weakness of human condition.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the emotional side of human life?
questions.answer: It portrays people as easily saddened and hurt by what happens around them.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a person’s ability to defend himself from all harm?
questions.answer: It says he does not have enough power to face every hardship and enemy.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the number of things a person needs?
questions.answer: It says his needs are many.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the burden of living?
questions.answer: Life places serious duties on a person even though he is not fully able to carry them.

questions.question: Why does losing familiar things cause ongoing pain?
questions.answer: Because human nature forms bonds with the world and with what it loves.

questions.question: What insight does the mind give a person, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It shows him lofty goals and lasting benefits.

questions.question: What does the image of a “short hand” suggest in the passage?
questions.answer: It suggests limited reach and inability to gain everything one wants or aims for.

questions.question: How does a short lifespan add to the human problem described here?
questions.answer: It leaves little time to fulfill all the high aims a person recognizes.

questions.question: Why is little patience important in understanding this passage?
questions.answer: It shows that a person not only lacks power and time but also struggles to endure difficulty for long.

questions.question: What complete understanding of a human being does this passage give?
questions.answer: A human being has deep hopes and connections, but he is weak, needy, limited, and often overwhelmed.

questions.question: What repeated pattern does the passage use to describe human beings?
questions.answer: It repeatedly shows a weakness in people and then contrasts it with a heavy challenge they face.

questions.question: Give one example of that contrast from the passage.
questions.answer: A person has little power, but he faces many troubles and enemies.

questions.question: What is another contrast related to human needs?
questions.answer: A person lacks much, yet his needs are still very many.

questions.question: What contrast appears in relation to work and responsibility?
questions.answer: A person is not very capable, but life’s duties are still heavy.

questions.question: How does the passage connect human relationships with sorrow?
questions.answer: Since a person is tied to many things in the world, their fading or loss causes pain.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the direction of human thought?
questions.answer: It says the mind reaches toward noble and lasting purposes.

questions.question: Why can this create frustration for a person?
questions.answer: Because his practical ability, lifespan, strength, and patience are too limited to match those aspirations.

questions.question: Does the passage present human limitation as only physical? Explain.
questions.answer: No. It includes emotional weakness, limited power, many needs, and restricted patience and time.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the human heart from this passage?
questions.answer: It becomes attached to people and things and suffers when they do not remain.

questions.question: What larger message about human life is built through these contrasts?
questions.answer: Human life is full of need and limitation, so people should recognize their dependence and not be deceived by pride.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens because a person is naturally weak?
questions.answer: He is affected by many things and often feels sorrow and grief.

questions.question: What makes human weakness harder to bear in this passage?
questions.answer: The large number of hardships and enemies makes that weakness more serious.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the human condition in terms of need?
questions.answer: It shows that people are lacking in many ways while also needing many things.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a person’s energy and skill compared with life’s demands?
questions.answer: It says people are limited and struggle while life places heavy responsibilities on them.

questions.question: How does human nature connect a person to the wider world?
questions.answer: It makes him related to the rest of creation, so outside changes affect him deeply.

questions.question: What kinds of changes in the world cause pain to a person?
questions.answer: The fading, loss, and disappearance of things he loves and is used to.

questions.question: What positive ability does reason give a person?
questions.answer: It lets him see noble goals and outcomes that last.

questions.question: What prevents that ability from solving all human problems?
questions.answer: A person still has limited reach, little time, weak strength, and small patience.

questions.question: How does the passage combine human honor and human weakness?
questions.answer: It shows that a person can recognize high purposes, yet still be fragile and unable to accomplish everything alone.

questions.question: What is a sound summary statement for the whole passage?
questions.answer: Human beings have high awareness and deep attachments, but they remain weak, needy, and limited in this life.
